cells.tense: You are here in the middle of the work, deciding what stays and what gets let go.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Call it yourself when something stings and nobody else is around to judge whether it was fair — then do the next thing you decided on before you sleep.
cells.core:
You can hold a hard feeling and still judge it cleanly. Under pressure, bearing what has to be borne, you can tell what someone owes from what they don't, and nothing reactive in you has to run the answer. That evenness is what lets you release what's finished and keep what still grows — and it's what the ones near you borrow without asking.

The unfairness usually gets settled by whoever complains loudest. Call it yourself, once, when something stings and nobody else is around to judge whether it was fair. Then do the next thing you decided on before you sleep, instead of a week of weighing. Whoever depends on you will feel the floor stay level. You might notice you already had the answer.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold a feeling and still judge it fairly.
cells.verb: Governing feeling with fairness so something can grow through what is released.
cells.place: Standing under a weight that you can hold and keep standing.

cells.tense: Your holding is running ahead of the moment, bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask what it's like for someone close to you when they're upset — then stay through the whole answer without reaching for anything that would make it better.
cells.core:
You keep watch over what the people closest to you are carrying, and the watch has grown bigger than they are. You're bracing for a weight nobody has picked up — the fix gets ready before the hurt lands, and those you're carrying for feel handled instead of met. The strength is real. It's just working at a distance now.

Ask what it's like for someone close to you when they're upset, then stay through the whole answer without reaching for anything that would make it better. No fixing, no managing. They'll still be in it afterward, and they'll have been in it with you beside them, which is the part they came for. You'll have put the weight down without leaving your post.
cells.sheetLine: You brace for the weight before anyone has picked it up.
cells.verb: Governing feeling with fairness so something can grow through what is released.

cells.tense: The moment already passed while you were still deciding whether to step through it.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: Pick what you'd actually like to be moving toward and give it a small piece of your day — on the days you can, stopping before it costs you.
cells.core:
Under pressure, bearing what has to be borne, the will underneath has gone quiet. You hold whatever arrives without complaint, and nothing you would have chosen for yourself is asking for anything back. What's left is endurance. It has stopped moving toward anything; it just stands under whatever comes.

Pick what you'd actually like to be moving toward and give it a small piece of your day, on the days you can, stopping before it costs you. Keep it going gently, the way you'd keep a fire alive without piling on wood. The first days it feels thin, and that's normal. What you're rebuilding is a direction you picked, so that holding what lands on you isn't the only muscle moving.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what arrives and ask for nothing back.
cells.verb: Governing feeling with fairness so something can grow through what is released.
cells.place: Standing under a weight that you can hold and keep standing.

cells.tense: You are already making the fair calls and filing them under how things happened.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Name one line this week — a small one — to whoever it concerns, and keep it past the first time it gets tested.
cells.core:
You decide what to keep and what to release, and you keep those near you steady while you do it — and when you describe it later, it sounds like things simply worked out. The decisions are yours. They get filed under circumstance, luck, the way the week went. You don't take the credit because you don't stop to notice a choice was made.

Name one line this week, a small one, to whoever it concerns. Then keep it past the first time it gets tested — the moment you'd usually let it slide to keep the peace. That's what makes it a line rather than a preference. Whoever hears it will hear a decision being made, which some of them already see; you'll hear it too, which is the part you've been skipping.
cells.sheetLine: The calls are yours, filed under how the week went.
cells.verb: Governing feeling with fairness so something can grow through what is released.
cells.place: Standing under a weight that you can hold and keep standing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is authorship in the Unacknowledged cell: I say the person is already making the fair calls and calling them ordinary luck, but the record only says the capacity is running without conscious integration, not that the calls are good or already happening. A reader could reasonably say 'no, I'm really not doing this yet — I ask other people what to do.' If that's the case the ask still works: deciding one small fairness for yourself teaches anyone something about where their judgment lives, even someone who's been outsourcing it. The sentence that serves the writer is 'The things and people in your orbit don't file it under luck' — it tells the person what they are rather than handing them something to look at, and it goes.
